title: Design Candidate F — in-Rust f32-FMA cascade for small-prime GEMM
description:
Add a new candidate strategy to the small-prime GEMM design (`dev/plans/small_prime_kernel_strategy.md`) and produce a per-(P, n) dispatch rule between it and the already-implemented Candidate C (16-bit-integer SIMD). ## Amendment — 2026-05-06 (user-approved post-R3) Criterion #3 (the per-(P, n) dispatch rule criterion) is amended to permit a degenerate uniform table when one candidate dominates at every (P, n) cell on the in-scope deployment surface. The original criterion text required a hybrid `n < N_thresh → F; n ≥ N_thresh → C` table; the empirical Wave-6B Candidate C bench (`dev/bench_results/2026-05-05-662f7a15-small-prime-gemm.csv`) plus Zen-3 micro-architectural analysis (Candidate F at 160 Gop/s vs Candidate C at 80 Gop/s with no upper crossover) falsified the hybrid hypothesis: there is no (P, n) regime on FMA3-capable hosts where C beats F. Candidate C is retained as the runtime fallback for non-FMA3 hosts (Zen 1, pre-Haswell), so the dispatch is genuinely between C and F — split by runtime CPU feature detection, not by (P, n). Per `CLAUDE.md` § *Success-criterion maturity markers* and the Wave-6A precedent (`5cacaec5` GF(251) `[hard]→[aspirational]` amendment), `[hard]` criteria can be amended in-loop when empirical evidence falsifies them. The aggregate contract (Candidate F is a single strategy with feasibility evidence per axis, dispatch wiring is concrete, Mersenne path preserved) still holds. ## Context (why this is needed now) The Wave-6B impl `662f7a15` landed Candidate C (AVX2 16-bit-integer-MAC SIMD) with measured GF(7)/GF(31) `[hard]` 1.5× FAIL at n ∈ {64, 256}³ (pass at n=1024³) and GF(251) `[aspirational]` soft-floor BREACH at n=256³ (28.7 Gop/s vs 40 Gop/s soft threshold). User-flagged 2026-05-06: the original Candidate D rejection (in-Rust f32 cascade) bundled the algorithm with the OpenBLAS dependency. A hand-rolled in-Rust AVX2 `_mm256_fmadd_ps` kernel uses the same f32-cascade algorithm without the OpenBLAS dep, and accesses Zen-3's 160 Gop/s f32-FMA peak (vs 80 Gop/s for the 16-bit-integer path). ## Success Criteria - [hard] `dev/plans/small_prime_kernel_strategy.md` is amended with a new § 4.5 Candidate F section: in-Rust AVX2 `_mm256_fmadd_ps` f32 cascade for $p \le 251$. The section follows the existing § 4.x structure (architectural pattern, mathematical sketch, inspiration, best fit). The amendment is added at-end with a "Amendment — 2026-05-06 (user-approved post-Wave-6B)" header in the new § block, mirroring the wave-6A amendment-block precedent. - [hard] § 5 (feasibility evidence) gains a § 5.5 Candidate F entry covering: (a) gf2-core kernels that would change, (b) MSRV / intrinsic-availability constraints, (c) interaction with Fp

Montgomery path, (d) interaction with kernel dispatch — same four-axis structure as § 5.1-§ 5.4. - [hard] § 6 (recommendation) gains an amendment block: instead of "Selected: Candidate C" being terminal, the recommendation becomes "Selected: hybrid Candidate C + Candidate F". Per the 2026-05-06 amendment above, the (P, n) rule may resolve uniformly to F when one candidate is shown to dominate at every (P, n) cell on FMA3-capable hosts. The dispatch retains Candidate C as the runtime fallback for non-FMA3 hosts. The rule must be supplied as a concrete decision table and a derivation citing the empirical CSV. - [hard] § 7 (implementation outline) is supplemented with § 7.4 covering Candidate F file-level changes (new `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/{fp_small_f32.rs, x86/fp_small_f32.rs}`, new `crate::simd::maybe_fp_small_f32` accessor, new dispatch branch in `try_simd_gemm_classical` keyed on the (P, n) selector with runtime FMA3 fallback to Candidate C). - [hard] § 9 self-satisfies the new criteria using the same self-satisfaction convention used in the Wave-6A close: the design pass produces evidence in-document; downstream impl `662f7a15-rework` consumes the dispatch rule. ## Out of scope - Candidate F implementation. That is `662f7a15`-rework. - f32 FMA kernel for $p > 251$ (medium-prime band) — that is `9e12659b` territory, which uses `_mm256_madd_epi16` u16-lane SIMD and is not blocked by this design pass. - f64-FMA cascade variants — only f32 is in scope here (matches fflas's `Modular` path; f32 mantissa 23 bits accommodates $k \cdot (p-1)^2 < 2^{23}$ for all $p \le 251$). ## Authority and references - **Authority document**: `dev/plans/small_prime_kernel_strategy.md` (commit `cd00161`+ R1-R4 fixes through `43393aa`). This issue amends it. - **Empirical motivation**: 662f7a15 worker bench output `dev/bench_results/2026-05-05-662f7a15-small-prime-gemm.csv` (the failing measurements). Cite verbatim. - **fflas algorithmic reference**: `dev/plans/fflas_ffpack_analysis.md` § 3 (BLAS integration pipeline) and design § 3 (existing reference algorithm survey). - **Hardware peaks**: Zen-3 single-core AVX2 throughput per Agner Fog instruction tables. Cited in the existing design § 6 #2. - **Follow-up consumer**: `662f7a15` will be re-dispatched for impl rework against the amended design after this issue closes. ## Deliverable shape A single commit on main amending `dev/plans/small_prime_kernel_strategy.md` with the new sections § 4.5, § 5.5, § 6 amendment, § 7.4, § 9 amendment. No source code changes. The amendment must use the existing maturity-marker convention (new criteria carry `[hard]` markers). After the design lands, `jit doc add` re-pins the doc to the new commit SHA on this issue, on `5cacaec5` (the parent design issue), on `662f7a15` (the impl), and on the parent epic `97bf0879`.
